subject: MedSol: customer-specific log purge variance & evidence pack
messages:
From: Andrew Burns <andrew.burns@medsol.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@medsol.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: variance to log purge window + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Stephanie,

We ran a compliance review and MedSol needs a customer-scoped exception to Redwood's default ephemeral log purge. Our standard requires 90 days of tenant debug/audit traces for incident correlation; your platform default is 30 days.

Request: can Redwood retain tenant-scoped inference logs (request/response metadata + counters, no PII) for 90 days for our tenant ID medsol-prod-01? This would be a policy carveout limited to our account and for production incidents only.

Also: our security team is completing SIG/CAIQ mappings for an upcoming SaaS evaluation. Can you provide the evidence artifacts you normally provide for:
- log retention policy and configurable TTLs
- proof of deletion / proof-of-delete process
- SOC 2 scope and any runbooks for temporary forensic preservation (how we request a hold)

Appreciate a quick note on feasibility and whether Redwood can do a scoped exception vs only offering a global policy change. Attaching our SIG questionnaire (redacted).

Thanks,
Andrew
Andrew Burns
Security Manager, MedSol
[attachment: medsol-sig-questions.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Burns <andrew.burns@medsol.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: variance to log purge window + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Andrew — thanks for the detail and for attaching the SIG. Short answer: we can support a tenant-scoped retention variance with operational controls, but there are tradeoffs and an approval path.

What I can do right now:
- Kick off an internal review and produce an evidence pack for SIG/CAIQ items you listed.
- Propose a scoped plan (technical and controls) for retaining only non-PII request/response metadata for 90 days. That plan will include encryption-at-rest boundaries and an export/erase playbook.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll route the variance request to our Privacy & Security review (Karthik and Laura are on this thread).
2) Karthik can outline the technical approach for limited retention (can be snapshot-based, encrypted, and tagged to your tenant).
3) Laura will confirm legal/contractual guardrails we need (SLA, audit access, termination behavior).

Timeline: I'll aim to have a preliminary retention-exception plan and a SIG evidence bundle by Tue 2027-04-20 EOD. If you need a formal approval earlier, call me and we can expedite.

Stephanie Nguyen
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

Andrew / Stephanie — quick technical summary and proposed safe path. Long version below; TL;DR: we can implement a tenant-level 90-day retention for a narrow class of logs (request metadata, inference metrics, non-content traces) using an encrypted snapshot bucket and time-bound access. Requires exec sign-off and a small ops runbook.

What we'd store (scope):
- request id, timestamp, model/version, latency/ms, token counts, routing metadata, error codes
- NOT stored: full prompt text, user PII, attachments, or any raw transcript flagged as sensitive by our PII filters

Implementation options (ordered by preference):
1) Encrypted tenant snapshot (recommended): create a tenant-tagged object store with DESKTOP-AES keys, retention 90d, exportable only via signed admin job. Snapshots require approval and are rotated monthly.
2) Extended short-term DB retention: extend the ephemeral store TTL for medsol-prod-01 to 90d with stricter access logging.

Controls we'll attach:
- Access restricted to named roles (Redwood Forensics, Redwood Ops) with Just-In-Time (JIT) approval flows.
- Audit trail of every preservation/export request (HubSpot ticket + signed approval).
- Auto-delete at end of retention; we'll generate a proof-of-delete digest you can request.

What I need from MedSol to proceed:
- Confirmation the requested scope excludes prompt/PII (explicitly acceptable)
- Point of contact for approvals and legal sign-off (name + email)
- Any additional regulatory constraints (e.g., must hold longer for incident under investigation)

I've attached a short plan for internal reviewers: retention-exception-plan.pdf.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: retention-exception-plan.pdf (application/pdf)]

Sara Lee (legal) — sara.lee@medsol.com

Andrew
